messages:
olivia-support: Hey team — AcmeCorp reporting intermittent 503s + very high tail latency on /v1/generate. They gave a request_id and local timestamp, asking us to hunt server logs and tell them if this was a gateway issue or an internal model timeout. @kyle-sre can you take a look?

raj-eng: Can you paste the full request_id + any example curl or headers they captured? also which region/cluster?

olivia-support: Request id: 0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123. Customer timestamp: 2026-03-12T15:04:22Z (UTC). Region: eu-west-1. Route: POST /v1/generate, model=redwood-alpha-1. They included this minimal curl:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

They also said the response headers had `x-rw-request-id: 0b3f...a123` and a high `x-rw-latency-ms` value (~4200).

kyle-sre: Thanks. First pass I'll run a KQL search over hot indices, expand +/- 2 minutes around 2026-03-12T15:04:22Z. Example KQL to run in Kibana:

```kql
@timestamp >= "2026-03-12T15:02:00Z" and @timestamp <= "2026-03-12T15:06:00Z" and (request_id : "0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123" or trace.id : "0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123")
```

Indices: logs-*, edge-logs-*, model-runtime-* . If nothing in hot indices check archived: logs-archived-YYYY.MM (we keep 30d hot + 90d cold). Cold retrieval can take ~20-40m and requires `archive:read` role.

maria-support: FYI customer is Dedicated (paid). SLA says we maintain 90d cold retention. I'll tell them we may need to pull the archive and will update them. Also ask them to send a debug bundle (headers + curl + local timestamp).

olivia-support: Sent request to customer for debug bundle. Asking them to include exact local request timestamp, full response headers, and if possible resend with `X-Request-ID` header set to the same id so we can correlate client logs.

raj-eng: For the debug bundle ask them to run this quick reproducible capture and attach output:

```bash
curl -i -s -D headers.txt -o body.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# attach headers.txt, body.txt and note local clock skew
```

kyle-sre: If we find nothing in logs by request_id, next steps: 1) search by client IP + user_agent + narrow time window, 2) check upstream LB logs (nginx/gateway) for 5xx at same time, 3) confirm model runtime metrics (OOM, P99 latencies). If it's an internal model timeout we'll likely see a stacktrace or a model exec cancellation in model-runtime logs.

diag-bot: Automated hint: request_id 0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123 currently resolves to no hot-log entry. Suggest run: `GET /archive/retrieve?index=logs-archived-2026.03&request_id=0b3fa4c2-9f12-4a6b-b2d1-8e77c9e5a123` (requires archive role).

maria-support: I'll open a ticket for archive retrieval and cc SRE. Olivia — once customer attaches the debug bundle I'll upload it to the ticket and ping @kyle-sre. Please also ask them to include any correlated request_ids from their side if they retried — retries produce new request_ids but we can tie via trace id if they set it. :+1:

kyle-sre: Got it. If archive returns nothing either, escalate to runtime-team with trace proof and the debug bundle. I'll post back here with the KQL results or archive status.

olivia-support: Thanks all — keeping customer updated. Will paste debug bundle link into this thread when received.
